messages:
Oncall-Bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] Elevated error rate on hosted inference (tool/function calls) observed since 17:12 UTC. Alerting eng-sre and oncall. thread=1782345678
Alex: seeing spike in fn-call errors and timeouts. 5xxs up from 0.3% -> 9% over last 7m. latency p95 up too.
Priya: confirmed. Structured-output endpoints have huge backpressure — queues for json-render worker processes are at 95% and growing.
Jordan: initial blast radius: ~12 customers, mostly high-throughput embedding+tool combos. A couple reported 502s in support tickets.
Maria: CS: calling those customers now, flagging potential degraded responses. No data loss reported, just failures/timeouts.
Alex: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable tool/function calling for non-SLA customers; 2) force fallback to plain text output (disable structured output) for high-throughput routes; 3) apply per-tenant rate caps for top N tenants until queue drains.
Priya: +1 to 2 and 3. Structured JSON serialization path is CPU/GPU memory heavy right now. If we fall back to text we avoid json-validate + schema rendering.
Jordan: I'll take lead on API gates. Alex do you want me to flip function-call_allow at the routing layer?
Alex: yes. Proposed sequence: a) apply soft rate-cap rule to top 10 tenants (50% of traffic) b) flip structured_output -> plain_text for endpoints tagged "realtime" c) disable external tool invocations (external HTTP/webhook tool calls) for hosted tier while we stabilize.
Liz: infra notes: we can patch routing config through control plane API. Command I plan to run:
```
# throttle top tenants
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/v1/rules -d '{"action":"rate_limit","targets":["tenant:top10"],"rate":"100rps"}'

# toggle structured output
curl -X PATCH -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/v1/features -d '{"structured_output":"off","scope":"realtime"}'

# disable tool calls globally for hosted
curl -X PATCH -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane.internal/v1/features -d '{"function_calls":"disabled","scope":"hosted"}'
```
Jordan: running the feature toggle now (will run sequentially). I'll post status.
Jordan: PATCH applied for structured_output scope=realtime -> off. (resp 200) reverting SDK flag.
Alex: good. Liz, can you apply the rate_limit rule and confirm which tenants get affected?
Liz: rate_limit POST accepted. Targets expanded: tenant:alpha, tenant:bravo, tenant:charlie, tenant:delta, tenant:echo, tenant:foxtrot, tenant:golf, tenant:hotel, tenant:india, tenant:juliet. All at 100rps.
Priya: monitoring shows queue depth starting to drop on json-renderers (95% -> 70% within 90s). Kernel memory usage down ~18%.
Maria: CS update: reached out to the top 6 customers in impacted list. Two customers (alpha, bravo) want temporary SLA exception; asked them to route lower-priority requests to batch endpoints.
Alex: good. Next: disable external webhooks/tools for hosted tier. Jordan/Liz coordinate.
Jordan: disabling external tool invocations now.
Jordan: API responded 200, feature function_calls disabled for scope=hosted. Hook invocations will now return 501 with helpful message.
Priya: we should set a warning banner in responses so integrators see why tooling is blocked. Suggest: "Tooling temporarily disabled due to system overload; retry later or use batch API"
Alex: agree. Jordan can you push response banner via gateway?
Jordan: banner pushed. Quick check: logs show 501s replacing previous 5xx spikes. error rate dropped to 2.1% overall. p95 latency trending down.
Maria: CS: customers notified of mitigation and expected ETA 30-45m to full recovery.
Liz: doing a slow rollback plan ready once stable: revert rate limits, re-enable structured_output for a small canary tenant, then re-enable toolcalls gradually.
Alex: handoff time in 20m — Priya you'll take the midnight oncall?
Priya: I can take the handoff. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and coordinate with infra.
Alex: thanks. final checklist before handoff: 1) monitoring alert thresholds adjusted so we don't get noisy alerts during drain (Jordan) 2) mitigation steps documented in incident ticket (Maria) 3) escalation path to eng-runtime if error rate creeps back above 5% (Liz)
Jordan: adjusted alert thresholds + silenced noisy alert group.
Maria: filed incident ticket INC-2026-314 with mitigation notes and customer list. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-314
Liz: infra will keep rate limits for 30m, then reduce restrictions to canary group.
Priya: taking over monitoring. leaving contact: priya@redwood (pager on). I'll update once we start re-enable canary.
Alex: thanks team — leaving handoff note: if any customer reports new 5xxs escalate to oncall immediately.
Oncall-Bot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: Priya (rotation: 18:00-02:00 UTC).
Priya: quick post-mit note: after 26m the json renderer queues normalized, CPU/mem stable, customers seeing reduced failures. I'll run canary re-enable for tenant:alpha in 10m and report.
Alex: done for now. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
